reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Eligibility and petition for common sewer district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 6 through A.L. 1992 H.B. 1803), and cross-reference note to section 249.451. Covers public-health necessity, eligible county classifications, multi-basin/municipality natural drainage area, federal aid eligibility under Title 33 U.S.C.A. § 1151 et seq., and county commission or charter-county executive/legislature petition to circuit court for commissioners and voter submission under sections 204.250 to 204.470.

headings.title: Contents of common sewer district petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and cross-reference note. Covers required petition contents: general territory description, suggested district name, and aim and purposes for creating the district.

headings.title: Eligibility for establishing a common sewer subdistrict
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Covers the 'notwithstanding' authorization to establish a subdistrict of an existing chapter 204 common sewer district for residential or commercial buildings in geographical proximity lacking available sanitary sewage disposal or treatment services, regardless of natural drainage area or basin, using subsections 4 to 7.

headings.title: Court-ordered subdistrict election, notice, approval, and ballot
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Covers circuit court order for good cause submitting subdistrict creation to real-property owners of record, required order/notice elements including the 25-percent cost and general obligation bond cap statement, voter approval matching Missouri Constitution Article VI § 26 general obligation bond thresholds, and substantially prescribed ballot wording; retains source phrasing shifting between owners of record, electors, and qualified voters.

headings.title: Alternative two-thirds property-owner petition for subdistrict
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Covers alternative subdistrict creation via circuit-court filing of a petition signed by owners of record of at least two-thirds by area of real property, with required project/cost/boundary/assessment contents, 7-day signature withdrawal cutoff notice, and 25-percent cost and general obligation bond cap notice.

headings.title: Court establishment order and preliminary plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Covers permissive circuit court order (after voter approval or proper petition) determining advisability, establishing the subdistrict, directing preliminary plans and specifications, making required findings, and stating the 25-percent cost/bond cap absent a new election or petition.

headings.title: Subdistrict boundary description and assessed area limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Covers describing subdistrict boundaries by metes and bounds, streets, or other sufficiently specific description, and limiting finally assessed subdistrict area to no more than the total area comprising 'such district'.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.250:10659, all seven subsections, history note (1967 through 1992 H.B. 1803), and cross-reference to section 249.451; verified all fingerprints. Checked county classifications, 33 U.S.C.A. § 1151 et seq. federal-aid condition, subdistrict election (noting archived shifts among owners of record, electors, and qualified voters) and Mo. Const. Art. VI § 26 approval threshold, two-thirds area petition alternative, 25-percent cap, and assessed-area limit ('such district'). Retained all seven titles as accurate.

headings.title: Voter-approval condition on taxes and bond-proceeds payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1803 § 3, A.L. 1993 S.B. 80, et al.). Bars the board over a subdistrict formed under section 204.250(3)-(7) from levying or collecting taxes to pay district indebtedness unless and until district or subdistrict voters authorize incurring indebtedness at an election, and permits paying subdistrict expenses and indebtedness from voter-authorized bond sales.

headings.title: Discretion regarding district funds for subdistrict
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. States rule of construction that the section neither prevents nor requires the board of trustees to expend common sewer district funds for the subdistrict's benefit.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.253:10662, both subsections, and history note (1992 H.B. 1803, 1993 S.B. 80); verified all fingerprints. Checked voter-approval bar on tax levies for section 204.250(3)-(7) subdistricts, permissive payment from voter-authorized bond sales, and rule of construction preserving board discretion over common sewer district funds. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Ten-percent assessed valuation bond limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1803 § 4). Limits total bonds issued under sections 204.251 to 204.257 for subdistrict improvements to 10 percent of assessed valuation of all taxable tangible property in the common sewer district.

headings.title: Bond execution, coupons, and sale conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers president signature, secretary attestation, district seal, facsimile secretary signature on interest coupons, and permissive bond sale under county road bond sale conditions.

headings.title: Bond registration, fund deposit, and warrant withdrawals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers registering section 204.251 to 204.257 bonds with the state auditor (as city bonds) and in the district secretary's registry book, depositing district moneys in board-designated banks, charging the treasurer, and drawing moneys by warrant for bond purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.254:10663, all three subsections, and 1992 H.B. 1803 history note; verified all fingerprints. Checked 10-percent common-sewer-district assessed-valuation cap on section 204.251-204.257 subdistrict bonds, signing/seal/coupon/county-road-bond sale terms, state-auditor and secretary registration, bank deposits, and warrant withdrawals. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Annual secretary certification of debt and operating costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 1803 § 5, A.L. 1993 S.B. 80, et al.). Covers the secretary's duty on or before May 15 annually to certify next-year maturing bond principal/interest and estimated subdistrict maintenance, facility rental/leasing, and necessary expenses to the board.

headings.title: Board tax levy and voter-approval proviso
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers board duty upon receiving the certificate to levy a sufficient tax on taxable subdistrict property, qualified by the proviso denying levy authority until district or subdistrict voters vote to incur such indebtedness.

headings.title: Tax extension, county collection, and statutory remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers extending the tax rate on tax books against taxable subdistrict property, collection and remittance by the county collector of revenue like state/county/school taxes, and applicability of state tax-collection laws, rights, and remedies.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.255:10664, all three subsections, and history note (1992 H.B. 1803, 1993 S.B. 80); verified all fingerprints. Checked May 15 annual secretary cost certification, board tax levy subject to the voter-approval indebtedness proviso, tax-book extension, county collector collection/remittance, and applicable state tax remedies. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Appointment and qualifications of sewer district commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 7, A.L. 1986 H.B. 1554 Revision). Covers circuit court appointment within 30 days of receiving the petition of three disinterested commissioners—one a licensed civil engineer or surveyor—to lay out and define proposed district boundaries.

headings.title: Boundary amendments, surveys, and maps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive commissioner power to alter or amend petitioned boundaries to include efficiently drainable areas or exclude unbenefitted natural drainage areas, and to have necessary surveys and maps made.

headings.title: Commissioner oath, hearing notice, and meeting place
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers commissioners qualifying by oath, publishing meeting notice at least five times in newspaper(s) at least 20 days prior to the meeting, and meeting at the courthouse of the county containing the major portion of the proposed district.

headings.title: Presiding commissioner, public hearing, and boundary determination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers the first-named commissioner presiding, the right of residents and real-property owners in or adjacent to the proposed district to be heard on boundaries, and majority commissioner determination fixing boundaries after the hearing.

headings.title: Hearing adjournments, commissioner pay, and stenographer-clerk
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers day-to-day hearing adjournments, circuit-court-determined commissioner compensation, and permissive employment of a stenographer and clerk at court-set compensation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.260:10667, all five subsections, and history note (1967, 1986 H.B. 1554 Revision); verified all fingerprints. Checked 30-day circuit court appointment of three disinterested commissioners (including licensed civil engineer or surveyor), boundary adjustments/surveys, oath and five-time/20-day published notice, public hearing, adjournments, and court-set commissioner and stenographer-clerk pay. Retained all five titles as accurate.

headings.title: Court order directing incorporation election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 9, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971). Covers circuit court order directing the county commission of any county partially within the proposed district to submit incorporation with court-approved boundaries to voters.

headings.title: County clerk certification of election results
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers each county clerk certifying election results for the proposed district portion within that county to the circuit court.

headings.title: Incorporation decree and single-county boundary adjustment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers decreeing incorporation of the full commissioners' area upon majority approval in each county, or altering boundaries to incorporate only the major-portion county when approved there but rejected in the other county.

headings.title: Petition dismissal and costs upon defeat
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers dismissing the petition and taxing proceeding and election costs against the petitioning county if the question fails to receive a majority in the major-portion county regardless of the other county's vote.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.280:10669, all four subsections, and history note (1967, 1978 H.B. 971); verified all fingerprints. Checked circuit court election order, county clerk certifications, multi-county incorporation vs. single-county boundary reduction, and petition dismissal with costs taxed to petitioning county upon defeat in major-portion county. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Corporate status and powers upon board organization
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 10). Covers becoming a body corporate and politic upon appointment and organization of the section 204.300 board of trustees, under the petitioned/decreed name, with power to sue and be sued, contract, acquire and hold property, and adopt a seal.

headings.title: Judicial notice of district existence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires all Missouri courts to take judicial notice of any district organized under sections 204.250 to 204.470.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.290:10670, both subsections, and 1967 history note; verified all fingerprints. Checked corporate/politic status and powers triggered upon section 204.300 board organization and mandatory judicial notice across Missouri courts for sections 204.250 to 204.470 districts. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Trustees, pay, and engineer except qualifying charter counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 11 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 4), and cross-reference to section 249.1100. Applies outside first-class charter counties containing all or part of a city of 350,000+ inhabitants; covers five appointed trustees plus adjoining-county chief executive, staggered five-year terms, 60-day board vacancy filling, outside-service pay under section 105.454, $100 attendance fees (2/month or 4/month in first-class counties; 1/week cap), expense reimbursement, staff/treasurer bond, and county sewer engineer or registered professional engineer. Explicitly notes archived source duplication: the four sentences on section 105.454 pay, attendance fees, and expenditure reimbursement appear twice verbatim in subsection 1.

headings.title: Trustees, pay, and administrator in qualifying charter counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and cross-reference to section 249.1100. Applies solely to first-class charter counties containing all or part of a city of 350,000+ inhabitants; covers the 10-member board (or 11-member two-county board with expense-only service), advisory board appointees under section 204.310, 60-day legislative appointment fallback, 10-member attendance fees/expenses/section 105.454 pay, staff, administrator as CEO exercising pre-September 28, 1983 chief engineer duties, and consulting engineers. Revised during review for parallel phrasing with subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.300:57310, both subsections, history note (1967 through 2025 S.B. 4), and cross-reference to section 249.1100; verified all fingerprints. Confirmed county-classification split around first-class charter counties with a 350,000+ city, 10- vs. 11-member board pay rules, pre-September 28, 1983 chief engineer duties transfer, and archived verbatim duplication of the four pay/attendance-fee/reimbursement sentences in subsection 1. Retained subsection 1; revised subsection 2 to 'Trustees, pay, and administrator in qualifying charter counties' for clean parallel structure.

headings.title: General management rules for any common sewer district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1967 p. 310 § 13, A.L. 1992 H.B. 948 merged with H.B. 1307; effective 2-18-92 and 4-7-92). Grants any common sewer district board power to pass necessary management and district-business rules and regulations.

headings.title: System and pretreatment rulemaking in qualifying charter counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (3)) and notes. Distinguished from subsection 1 by applying to first-class charter counties with a city of 350,000+ inhabitants; grants primary authority (subject to clean water commission authority/rules under section 644.026) over sewer systems/treatment facilities, industrial users, and POTW pretreatment programs including additional pretreatment requirements.

headings.title: Territorial reach and enforcement of subsection 2 rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Makes rules adopted under subsection 2 applicable and enforceable by civil, administrative, or other actions within any served territory and against municipalities, subdistricts, districts, or industrial users discharging directly or indirectly.

headings.title: Authority cumulative with constitutional, statutory, and agency powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Provides that section authority is in addition to and not in derogation of Missouri constitutional/statutory, federal water pollution control, or agency authority.

headings.title: Definition of industrial user
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Defines 'industrial user' for this section and section 204.300 (archived cross-reference to section 204.300 retained faithfully without correction, though 'industrial user' does not appear in section 204.300), covering Clean Water Act § 307(b)-(d) sources, SIC divisions A, B, D, E, or I, solid/hazardous waste operations, and offsite aqueous waste facilities discharging to the district system.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.320:10673, all five subsections including subdivisions (1)-(3), and history/effective-date notes (1967, 1992 H.B. 948 / H.B. 1307, effective 2-18-92 and 4-7-92); verified all fingerprints. Checked contrast between general districts (subsection 1) and qualifying first-class charter counties (subsection 2, mandatory 'shall' subject to section 644.026 clean water commission authority), territorial enforcement, cumulative authority, and archived subsection 5 cross-reference to section 204.300 (retained without alteration). Retained all five titles as accurate.

headings.title: Surveys and general plan for district facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1967 p. 310 § 14 through A.L. 1992 H.B. 948 merged with H.B. 1307; effective 2-18-92 and 4-7-92). Covers board duty to conduct surveys and lay out the general plan for acquiring/constructing land, rights-of-way, sewers, treatment facilities, and extensions or improvements.

headings.title: Discharge agreements, clean water commission disputes, and enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Covers permissive discharge and hazardous-waste agreements with municipalities, subdistricts, private districts, or industrial users, mandatory referral of unresolved disputes to the clean water commission for binding determination, waste-control duties, and circuit court compliance petitions and continuing jurisdiction.

headings.title: Contracts for proportionate treatment costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes board contracts with each participating community for payment of its proportionate share of treatment costs.

headings.title: Connection and use contracts inside or outside district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Authorizes contracts with public agencies, individuals, private corporations, and political subdivisions inside and outside the district to connect with and use district facilities on board-determined terms and rates regardless of natural drainage area or basin.

headings.title: Refusing noncompliant wastes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Authorizes the board to refuse wastes not meeting relevant state or federal water pollution, solid waste, or pretreatment standards.

headings.title: Powers over individual home or business treatment systems
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Grants necessary and convenient powers, including rulemaking, to operate, maintain, administer, and regulate individual home sewage or business treatment systems within district jurisdiction.

headings.title: Facility operations, pretreatment powers, fines, and enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 (subdivisions (1) to (6)) and notes. Grants treatment facility and pretreatment program powers regarding discharging municipalities, subdistricts, districts, and industrial users, including rules/ordinances, orders, permits, civil administrative fines up to $1,000 per violation per day on industrial users, circuit court legal/equitable actions, and petitioning county prosecutors for criminal proceedings.

headings.title: Procedural remedies for orders, permits, fines, and penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Authorizes board rules creating procedural remedies—including time to respond, show cause, and request reconsideration of fines or penalties—for persons affected by board orders, permits, fines, or penalties.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for false statements and monitoring tampering
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and notes. Sets first-conviction (up to $1,000/day and/or 1 year) and second-conviction (up to $3,000/day and/or 3 years) penalties for knowing false statements/certifications or falsifying/tampering with required monitoring devices or methods, without precluding civil remedies.

headings.title: Delegated actions by the executive officer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and notes. Provides that references in this section to actions by the board of trustees include delegated actions by its executive officer.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.330:10675, all ten subsections including subsection 7 subdivisions (1)-(6), and history/effective-date notes (1967 through 1992 H.B. 948 / H.B. 1307, effective 2-18-92 and 4-7-92); verified all fingerprints. Verified exact distinctions from section 204.618, including subsection 7 administrative fines up to $1,000/day and criminal prosecution referrals, subsection 8 fine/penalty reconsideration remedies, and subsection 9 criminal penalties for false statements and monitoring tampering. Retained all ten titles as accurate.

headings.title: Eminent domain within district and pre-condemnation surveys
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 15, A.L. 1983 H.B. 371). Grants board right to condemn property within the district under chapter 523 for sewer/treatment structures, plus private-land pre-condemnation survey entry authority granted to railroads under section 388.210.

headings.title: Property acquisition and condemnation in certain first-class counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes boards in first-class noncharter counties of 145,000 to 150,000 population to purchase, receive by gift, lease, rent, or condemn (under chapter 523) real or personal property both within and without the district.

headings.title: Crossing or using public streets, roads, and parks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants conditional right to cross, follow, or traverse public streets, roads, alleys, parks, or places upon filing occupancy maps and non-interfering work plans with the county commission or mayor having immediate jurisdiction.

headings.title: District responsibility for work and restoration costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the district to bear the entire expense of works and restoring occupied ground as nearly as possible to its former condition.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.340:10678, all four subsections, and history note (1967, 1983 H.B. 371); verified all fingerprints. Checked chapter 523 condemnation and section 388.210 pre-condemnation survey entry within district (subsection 1), within/without acquisition and condemnation for first-class noncharter counties of 145,000-150,000 population (subsection 2), conditional public-way crossing, and district work/restoration expense responsibility. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Bidding and exceptions for construction over $500
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 16). Requires letting trunk sewer and treatment plant construction contracts exceeding $500 under sections 204.250 to 204.470 to the lowest responsible bidder after at least 20 days' published notice, excepting repairs or emergencies requiring prompt attention, with authority to reject all bids and readvertise. Revised during review to explicitly reflect the repair/emergency exceptions.

headings.title: Professional survey, mapping, planning, and superintendence agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes agreements (with advisory board concurrence) with competent persons, firms, or corporations for surveys, maps, plans, laying out, and superintendence of work under sections 204.250 to 204.470, capped at one piece or class of work per agreement.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.350:10679, both subsections, and 1967 history note; verified all fingerprints. Checked $500 trunk-sewer/treatment-plant bidding threshold, repair/emergency exception, 20-day notice, bid rejection, and advisory-board-concurred professional survey/mapping/planning/superintendence agreements limited to one piece or class of work. Revised subsection 1 to explicitly reflect repair/emergency exceptions; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Eligibility for contiguous boundary extensions and non-overlap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 371). Authorizes extending boundaries of a district organized under sections 204.250 to 204.470 to include contiguous efficiently serviceable areas, excluding territory within any other sewer district.

headings.title: Trustee or resident petition to circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive trustee filing—and mandatory filing upon petition of 25 or more residents within the district or proposed addition—of a circuit court boundary-extension petition setting out reasonableness/necessity, boundary lines, and prayer.

headings.title: Hearing schedule and published newspaper notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers court fixing hearing time and circuit clerk publishing notice stating proposed extension boundaries in a county newspaper for three consecutive weeks beforehand.

headings.title: Hearing findings, boundary changes, decree, or dismissal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers court findings on public health, welfare, or utility/benefit, rendering a favorable decree (with authority to alter proposed extension boundaries), or dismissing the petition.

headings.title: Order for annexation election and territory notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers court order directing the appropriate election authority to hold an election in both the original sewer district and proposed territory, with notice describing the annexed territory.

headings.title: Ballot form for boundary annexation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Sets forth the ballot question form for annexing the contiguous area described in the election notice.

headings.title: Certification of results and final court decree
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Covers election authority certifying results and circuit court decreeing extended boundaries—or declaring failure and unchanged boundaries—based on a combined majority vote across the original district and proposed territory.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.355:10680, all seven subsections, and 1983 H.B. 371 history note; verified all fingerprints. Checked contiguous-area boundary extension rules, non-overlap bar, permissive trustee / mandatory 25-resident petition, three-week notice, hearing decree/dismissal, combined-area majority election, ballot form, and final court decree. Retained all seven titles as accurate.

headings.title: Voter or customer bond approval in certain counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 18, A.L. 1978 H.B. 971, A.L. 2001 H.B. 501). Bars common sewer districts in qualifying first-class charter counties (city of 350,000+) or noncharter first-class counties (63,700 to 75,000) from issuing sewerage revenue bonds without majority voter assent or written assent of three-quarters of customers, and defines 'customer'. Explicitly records source catchline-versus-body discrepancy: the official catchline states 'four-sevenths vote', whereas the archived body requires 'a majority of the voters' or 'three-quarters of the customers'. Revised during review to reflect the qualifying-county scope.

headings.title: Ballot form for revenue bond proposition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets forth the substantially prescribed ballot wording for submitting the common sewer district revenue bond proposition.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.370:10682, both subsections including subsection 1 subdivisions (1)-(2), and history note (1967, 1978 H.B. 971, 2001 H.B. 501); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed catchline-versus-body discrepancy: official catchline cites 'four-sevenths vote' while archived body requires 'a majority of the voters' or written assent of 'three-quarters of the customers' in qualifying first-class charter (city 350,000+) or noncharter (63,700-75,000) counties. Revised subsection 1 to reflect qualifying-county scope while remaining faithful to the body; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Issuance resolution, advisory concurrence, and required recitals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1967 p. 310 § 19, A.L. 1983 H.B. 371). Covers issuing election-authorized revenue bonds by board resolution with prior advisory board concurrence under sections 204.250 to 204.470, and required cost-estimate and bond-detail recitals.

headings.title: Optional prior redemption terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits bonds to include provisions for redemption prior to maturity, with or without premium, on board-determined times and conditions.

headings.title: Interest rate under 108.170 and thirty-five-year maturity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires revenue bonds to bear interest in accordance with section 108.170 and mature within 35 years from date.

headings.title: Bearer, registered, and coupon bond forms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits bearer, registered, or coupon bonds and registration privileges for principal and interest or principal only as provided by resolution.

headings.title: Bond signatures and validity despite office changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers officer signing of bonds and coupons as directed by resolution and continued validity even if an officer ceases holding office before delivery or did not hold office on the ascribed bond date. Revised during review to cover both ceasing to hold office before delivery and not holding office on the ascribed date.

headings.title: Sale price floor, interest limit, and subordinate bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers board sale terms subject to a 90-cents-on-the-dollar price floor and section 108.170 interest-cost ceiling on actual proceeds, and permits authorizing junior or subordinate revenue bonds.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.380:10684, all six subsections, and history note (1967, 1983 H.B. 371); verified all fingerprints. Checked election-authorized bond resolution with advisory board concurrence, optional prior redemption, section 108.170 interest and 35-year maturity, bond forms, officer-change signature validity (both ceasing office before delivery and not holding office on ascribed date), and 90-cents sale floor/subordinate bonds. Revised subsection 5 to cover both office-change scenarios; retained subsections 1-4 and 6.

headings.title: Pledge of system net revenues to bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1967 p. 310 § 22 through A.L. 1992 H.B. 948; effective 2-18-92). Automatically pledges a sufficient amount of sewerage system net revenues to pay principal and interest on revenue bonds issued under sections 204.250 to 204.470.

headings.title: Definition of net revenues
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Construes 'net revenues' as all income and revenues from system ownership and operation minus actual and necessary operation and maintenance expenses.

headings.title: Treasurer duty to pay principal and interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Imposes a mandatory duty on the common sewer district treasurer to provide for prompt payment of maturing revenue bond principal and accruing interest.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.410:10687, all three subsections, and history/effective-date notes (1967 through 1992 H.B. 948, effective 2-18-92); verified all fingerprints. Checked statutory net-revenue pledge under sections 204.250 to 204.470, 'net revenues' definition, and mandatory treasurer payment duty. Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Separate system revenue and reserve accounts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (7)) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1967 p. 310 § 23, A.L. 1992 H.B. 948; effective 2-18-92). Permits bond resolutions under sections 204.250 to 204.470 to allocate system revenues into separate accounts for operations/maintenance, debt service, depreciation/replacements, debt reserve, contingencies, extensions/improvements, and other desirable purposes.

headings.title: Limits on additional bonds and bondholder covenants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Permits bond resolutions to limit issuance of additional system revenue bonds or their holders' rights and to include bondholder agreements, covenants, or restrictions securing payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.420:10688, both subsections including subsection 1 subdivisions (1)-(7), and history/effective-date notes (1967, 1992 H.B. 948, effective 2-18-92); verified all fingerprints. Checked permissive bond-resolution allocation into separate revenue/reserve accounts and permissive additional-bond limitations and bondholder covenants. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Delinquent charges, interest, property liens, and enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 371, A.L. 1984 H.B. 1590). headings.title: Inclusion of section 204.300(2) board of trustees

headings.title: Permissive reassessment or new assessment if invalid or excessive
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes ('may') reassessment or new assessment upon original-style notice and hearing if a court sets aside an assessment, the governing body finds it excessive, or counsel advises in writing it is or may be invalid. Explicitly notes catchline-versus-body discrepancy: the official catchline states 'required, when', whereas the archived body uses permissive 'may'. Revised during review to explicitly reflect permissive 'may'.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 204.664:10756, both subsections, and 2007 S.B. 22 history note; verified all fingerprints. Checked no-notice supplemental assessments for total-cost errors capped at 25 percent without a new petition (subsection 1) and confirmed catchline-versus-body discrepancy in subsection 2: official catchline states 'required, when', whereas archived body uses permissive 'may' for reassessment or new assessment after judicial invalidation, excess finding, or written counsel invalidity advice. Retained subsection 1; revised subsection 2 to explicitly reflect permissive 'may'.
